question: What economic policies did Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi propose in 2025?
text:
In 2025, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi proposed what she called **“responsible and proactive” fiscal policy**: use government spending and tax relief to ease the cost-of-living squeeze, while investing in industries that could raise wages and strengthen Japan’s economy. She argued that faster growth would help bring down the government debt-to-GDP ratio. ([japan.kantei.go.jp](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/104/statement/202510/24shoshinhyomei.html?utm_source=openai))

- **Cost-of-living relief.** Her cabinet’s November 21 package included winter electricity and gas subsidies, a **¥20,000 payment per child**, and grants for local governments to tailor relief. It also called for ending the provisional gasoline tax surcharge on December 31, 2025, and the diesel surcharge on April 1, 2026. ([japan.kantei.go.jp](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/104/statement/202511/21kaiken.html?utm_source=openai))
- **Higher take-home pay.** The December tax reform plan proposed raising the minimum income-tax threshold to **¥1.78 million** and adjusting basic deductions for inflation. Takaichi also proposed developing refundable tax credits for low- and middle-income earners. A separate idea in the October coalition agreement—a two-year suspension of the consumption tax on qualifying food and beverages—was not part of the November relief package. ([mof.go.jp](https://www.mof.go.jp/tax_policy/tax_reform/outline/fy2026/08taikou_gaiyou.htm?utm_source=openai))
- **Investment and wage growth.** She proposed public-private investment in **17 strategic sectors**, including AI, semiconductors, shipbuilding, quantum technology and aerospace. The plan also aimed to secure critical supply chains and help smaller businesses improve productivity so they could sustain wage increases that outpaced inflation. ([japan.kantei.go.jp](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/104/actions/202512/01fii_priority.html?utm_source=openai))

The November package comprised **¥21.3 trillion in new fiscal measures**, or **¥25.5 trillion** including government investment and loan programs. The Diet passed the supplementary budget backing the package in December. ([japan.kantei.go.jp](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/104/statement/202511/21kaiken.html?utm_source=openai))
